scope: Confirmed remaining-push-ssrf application fix; three existing source files and two focused tests only. No commit, push, merge, deployment, dependency, CI, infrastructure, or migration changes.
finding: An authenticated browser subscription previously accepted internal HTTPS targets and web-push reached https.request for 127.0.0.1:8443. Original no-egress proof retained in /tmp/obligon-remaining-access-proof.json.

files.change: Shared endpoint/key validator at registration and delivery; exact documented FCM/Mozilla origins and documented Apple/Microsoft subdomains, HTTPS/default port only, no credentials/fragment/whitespace/backslash. Canonical URL and base64url keys. P-256 curve point validation. Native HTTPS agent with guarded single DNS lookup, four global sockets, DNS deadline, socket idle timeout; invalid rows skipped with redacted reason, expired rows deleted only for user.
Reject invalid subscriptions before DB writes. Remove both original/canonical endpoint spelling only for caller. Preserve idempotent unknown removal and actual query errors.

Surface API/service-worker/browser unsubscribe errors to existing preference caller. False unsubscribe result is successful only when browser no longer has subscription. Existing subscribe rejection already propagated.
7 isolated helper tests, including failure propagation and expired subscription handling.

acceptanceCriteria: Unapproved HTTP/HTTPS/IP/private/loopback/encoded IP/IPv6/userinfo/port/suffix-confusion/fragment/control URL variants are not stored and cannot reach web-push or https.request.
Documented browser push service fixture subscriptions and valid P-256/auth keys still store and deliver through mocked HTTPS only.
Malformed, wrong-length, invalid-point, invalid-base64, and incorrect-padding keys are rejected before storage/provider.
Each outgoing socket gets only checked public DNS addresses from its one lookup; private/mixed/special-purpose answers and stale late answers fail closed.
web-push 3.6.7 rejects redirects and no private Location target is followed.
Invalid stored subscription diagnostic omits endpoint capability, keys, and notification payload.
Removal is scoped to caller, survives canonical URL spelling, and unknown/expired removal remains idempotent; actual failure is surfaced.

primarySources.use: Google browser PushSubscription example uses https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/ opaque token.
Mozilla notification URL is opaque and provider reserves future path changes.
Apple tells managed push endpoint servers to allow any subdomain of push.apple.com.
Apple reiterates *.push.apple.com for Safari standards-based Web Push.
WNS CloudServiceDNS *.notify.windows.com and port443 for servers sending notifications.
Current Microsoft Edge policy identifies its built-in WNS push client connecting to Windows Push Notification Service; hostname source is separate WNS official configuration documentation.
Existing library documents HTTPS Agent option and socket timeout; pinned local 3.6.7 source inspected to confirm non-2xx/redirect rejection and direct https.request.
Native HTTPS Agent options, preserving default TLS verification and SNI host.
Native BlockList.addSubnet/check; used APIs available in Node14.18+, not recent26-only APIs.
Web Push authentication secret16bytes and uncompressed P-256 representation65bytes.
Conservative IPv4 special-purpose range exclusions including private/shared/link-local/loopback/docs/benchmark.
Conservative IPv6 global-unicast-only with protocol/documentation/6to4 exclusions.

changedContracts: Subscribe returns400 for unsupported/self-hosted providers or malformed keys; supported existing browser service origins remain accepted.
Explicit443/encoded hostname and valid optional base64url padding normalize before storage/send. Unsubscribe matches original and canonical endpoint.
DNS rejects a whole response containing any non-public address; intentional split-horizon provider DNS cannot be used.
sendPush remains best-effort delivered boolean; disallowed stored rows are retained for owner removal and skipped on each delivery.
disableWebPush now rejects service-worker/API/browser removal failure so existing caller can keep preference and show error; missing/expired subscriptions are successful disabled end states.

limits: No outbound private/provider request, real browser permission, actual provider registration, DNS query, payment activity, deployment, or production smoke test performed. Tests stub DB/provider/DNS boundaries; redirect/encryption use real installed web-push with https.request intercepted.
Test process isolation was blocked in this restricted sandbox; --test-isolation=none produced the read 82API+23web tests all passing with0skips. Root owns full-suite/build verification.

Socket timeout bounds inactivity, not complete response wall-clock duration. DNS lookup has a deadline; four total outgoing sockets cap concurrency. Library response-body/queue-total limits remain unchanged.
Trust remains in vendor-controlled documented DNS namespaces and normal TLS/CA validation; IPv4 special-purpose and IPv6 non-global ranges intentionally conservative.
A browser's currentPushState checks local subscription state, not API stored-row state; existing enable failure propagates to caller, but no new remote state endpoint was added.
Endpoint provider hostnames can change; unsupported new browser providers require reviewed allowlist maintenance based on primary sources.
